recs.name: Atop the Skyscrapers
recs.tag: Not all wishes have an outcome.

lines.x: Aha, how many are you? Five, no, six, huh? I'm in a hurry, so just take me all at once!
In the alleys of Lungmen, Exusiai is making deliveries in her own special way, as usual.
What she doesn't know is that on a rooftop not far away, someone is watching her.
Tsk tsk, El is playful as ever, and her marksmanship continues to improve.
You think so too, right? Watching her makes me miss my gun.
Get Rhodes Island to make a gun-staff? Perish the thought... If Lemuen saw, she'd make fun of me.
Besides, wouldn't that look like I'm pining for the past?
Hm? I'm not that sentimental.
But it's not like I've forgotten either.
Times change, and so do people. I thought you'd know that better than anyone.
...That's true. You perceive things different from we do, huh.
I do think about it sometimes. What does change feel like when you count time by the century?
Can you find meaning in a subtle feeling at all?
I mean, you know it doesn't matter to me anyway.
Oh, so it was you, Mostima.
Yith?
G'day.
Does Emperor need me for something?
Not really. There hasn't been anything major lately. I was just passing by when I felt a familiar aura.
And that's... Exusiai over there? I see, I see, just another day of work.
That's right. Also took the chance to take this little fella out for some fresh air and a little chat.
Ah, sounds like a good time. I'm jealous.
What about you?
Same as always. No rest for the wicked.
You work too hard.
Oh, please. It's what I was made for.
By the way, since you're here, I'd like to ask you a favor.
Let's hear it.
I've got a nasty complainer here lately. Might be something wrong with the lock. I was hoping you'd take a look for me.
Ah, I thought the lock was looking a bit worn down when you gave it to me for safekeeping last Sauin. Wouldn't surprise me if there were some minor problems.
Pass it over then, I'll take care of it.
Your other one's fine?
Sure, it's in the lock. The other one's just the key. Won't give me any issues.
Mostima pats the gray staff at her waist, then draws the brown staff out and hands it to Yith.
Old friend, we meet again.
...Huh, looks like it's in a bad mood indeed, and doesn't want to talk to me.
It happens.
Speaking of which, Mostima, I've never asked you this before, but I'm curious - where did you get this lock and key?
It was somewhere around Kazdel before it came into my hands.
Near Kazdel, huh... That explains a lot.
Can't say I expected that.
If you want more details, I mean, I could tell you the whole story. But I don't really feel like it.
The whole story... Are you talking about the Liberi girl?
Yeah, you've met?
Just once, last Sauin.
Pain in the ass, isn't she?
Yea...
'Bang!' Suddenly, a crossbow bolt penetrates into the space between Mostima and Yith.
See?
Seems like she's no fan of mine.
No, she's just getting pissy at me. Any other questions?
Really dig deep there. I joined Penguin Logistics because of you and Emperor, but we haven't had any serious talks since then.
So hit me with any questions you got.
Have you considered looking for the other pieces?
This is the only one left.
And even if it wasn't, it's not into the idea, and neither am I. Might as well leave things as they are.
You know though, if it really wasn't interested, it wouldn't have ended up like this in the first place.
I see. That does make sense.
Much of the way we are now can be attributed to similar decisions.
Actually, I've asked it before, whether it wanted to come out.
Let me think... That's right, it was during the Rhodes Island operator test.
Why?
Umm... I guess because it seemed like an interesting place, so I wanted to show them what I could do?
Might've also been because I wanted to scare the Doctor.
This one wouldn't cooperate, though. It felt something, I guess.
And hey, I gotta hand it to 'em, Rhodes Island is definitely interesting. You should check it out yourself, if you have the time.
Yes, if I have the time.
And when might that be?
Who knows? Keep an eye on Emperor's mood. If it sours, I might have some time on my hands.
But meetings between people are wonderful things indeed.
After its hibernation, it actually met a wielder so well suited to it.
Maybe.
But if I'm being real, it's brought me way more headaches than power.
But you don't mind, do you?
Guess I don't.
In any case, that's enough chatting for the day.
I'll let you know how the staff turns out.
Alright. Bye bye.
What's with the pissy face?
You.
I'm honored.
Who the hell was that? I know Emperor's got something crazy going on underneath, but I never knew Penguin Logistics had anyone like that.
You actually gave him your staff, and he seemed pretty comfortable with it.
Let's say it's his area of expertise and he's trustworthy.
Let's say your trust and that crossbow bolt have a conversation.
Do you need an explanation? I'm an open book.
No thanks... 'they' obviously know what's going on, and just decided not to tell me.
And that means I shouldn't be hearing it from you.
And that doesn't bother you at all?
My job is to keep my eyes on your horns. Beyond that, it's none of my business.
You don't care at all?

Hey, hear me out. You volunteered to watch me, way back when, but there's a ton of stuff you have no way of knowing. And you're running yourself ragged to keep up with me. That's some serious masochism.
As if I need you to spell it all out.
I'll say it again: what happened in Kazdel wasn't your fault.
Whether you were there or not, I would've pulled the trigger.
And you don't care that you've turned into this, I take it?
Bingo! See, you're getting to know me better and better.
And my choices are none of your business.
Sure, sure— Oh yeah, some folks from the Notarial Hall swung by yesterday, right? Another new job?
Not for the time being, just a routine report. But...
Oh? Did they change your codename again?
Yeah... *Sigh*.
That bad, huh? Lay it on me, I could use some cheering up.
...One-Armed Chainsaw Guy.
Huh... Did they just watch that shitty Lungmen flick?
I brought it back. Ugh, I should've known better. Why didn't I bring them something artsy?
Hah, hah, hah. Maybe you'll be Guns n' Roses next time.
Better than One-Armed Chainsaw Guy.
Alright, let's go.
I thought you were going to follow her around all day.
Do I look that bored to you?
If you ask me, I'd say that there aren't many people in this world more bored than you.
Do you really think so highly of me?
That wasn't a compliment.
What matters is that I take it as a compliment.
Anyway, that really wasn't my plan. Just had to swing by to take a look, call it force of habit. Wouldn't be my first time doing this either, and you should know that.
I do. That you're not proactively trying to make contact with her is a good thing in my opinion, but...
Ever since I had that little chat with her last Sauin, you've been totally fixated on it.
Are you worried that I'll tell her something?
If that was your plan, I might not be able to stop you. So I need to know how you feel about it.
Hmm... Fine then.
I know that look in your eyes. You're not gonna leave until I give you an answer.
I'm glad you understand.
Force speaks louder than reason with you.
Tell me this... what's the best way to make someone stop caring about you?
To disappear from their life.
No, not good enough. Once you've appeared, there's no way to completely disappear.
You have to wait for that person to find a new life, a new environment.
To tell the truth, I never thought she'd come running here from Laterano.
When Emperor told me she joined Penguin Logistics, I was quite shocked.
But you know, that whole time until Sauin, I never once spoke to her.
As for what happened then... Just consider it part of the festivities.
She's not going to give up looking for you.
But she's not actually looking for me.
It's not like she had anything to do with it, at least not directly, but we all have to keep our mouths shut.
Is that something I can clue her in on? Tell me, One-Armed Chainsaw Guy.
Please don't unironically call me that name.
Unfortunately, it's absolutely top secret, so you cannot.
See, I can't tell her the thing she wants to know the most, so what's the point of me showing up in her life?
Give her little hints here and there, pique her interest, and drag her into this whole mess?
So, you want her to stop caring about you?
Isn't that what you want too?
As I said, from an official standpoint, I'd like her to distance herself from any matters concerning you. Personally speaking though, I don't really care.
Honestly, if you were to ask me if that's really what I want, I don't think I'd say yes.
But when I let go of Laterano, cut all my ties, it was just as easy as when I raised my gun that one time. No hesitation.
All I can say is, if something happens, just let it be.
That is indeed the kind of person you are, and I don't like it. You don't care about loss.
Lots of people dislike that about me.
But color me interested. What good comes from caring about loss?
You end up crying your eyes out over whatever you've lost and whatever you see yourself losing, and then what?
I'm not here to talk philosophy with you. All I'll say is, if you really think that, then why did you come to watch her?
Take a guess?
No clue. I don't suppose you're lame enough to be doing this in hopes that she'll realize you're here.
You haven't been reading sappy romance novels, have you? Go easy on that stuff.
Grrr!
Oh, did Lemuen ever tell you why El is named after her? Why is her name Lemuel when the two of them are obviously not blood-related?
She keeps her work and her home life separate.
True.
The reason's simple. When she joined that family, El hadn't been born yet, and the parents decided it would be nice to integrate her into the family.
Though, that couple is just as joyous as El. If you told me they were just too lazy to come up with another name, I'd probably buy that.
In any case, Lemuen might not straight up say it, but she's really grateful to those parents, deep down.
And she cared even more about her little sister Lemuel.
So what does that have to do with anything you're doing here?
I'll spell it out for you, One-Armed Chainsaw Guy.
I'm thinking that Lemuen would let Lemuel leave Laterano, not just because she wanted to.
She's a discerning one. If El really got obsessed with you-know-what, I don't think she would've let her go.
It is precisely because that matter had nothing to do with El, and because finding me is not some obsession she can't give up—
—that she could come to Lungmen and join Penguin Logistics.
What Lemuen really wants is for El to see the world and find her own life.
And she kind of indirectly handed the responsibility to look after El over to me.
Even though you left without saying goodbye?
Precisely because I left without saying goodbye.
Watching her from a distance probably doesn't count as 'looking after.'
It's not like I left Penguin Logistics because of her either. It's something I should've done from the beginning, right?
So you're doing all this because you believe it's what Lemuen wants you to do?
Who knows.
Might've just been an excuse I came up with to explain why I'm doing this.
Well that's a surprise. I never expected you to come up with such a sentimental excuse.
I'm not a robot. There just happens to be a whole lot of stuff I don't care about.
Guilt, nostalgia, sorrow, etcetera etcetera. My heart's packed full of 'em all, but I've got them smoothed out pretty good now.
But if you or Lemuen decided to cut ties with me or something, I'd feel pretty sad.
For how long?
Dunno, I could probably manage a week, yeah?
That's a damn long time.
From ten-thousand feet, you could say I also grew up with those sisters. Since El came here, it's only natural I'd keep an eye out for her.
So, you plan to keep going along like this?
More or less? She seems to be getting on just fine with her current partners.
I do think we'll meet once in a pair of blue moons, here or there, but only out of happenstance. That's good enough for you, isn't it?
That's fair...
...is what I'd like to say, though from a personal perspective, I don't think it'd be fair to her, even if I'm not qualified to say it.
I guess. But ever since I became the owner of the lock and key, fairness has kind of left my vocabulary.
If I've got a reason to talk to her, I'm not gonna dodge it. If there is something I have to tell her, I'll deliver the message in person.
But the truth is... I don't have a reason, or anything like that.
I have my mission, and this girl already found a new life in this city.
Don't you think that's actually fair, in a sense?
As long as you're fine with the status quo.
Alright, shoo already. If someday, by some stroke of ill fortune, she ends up getting tangled in our side's mess, we can pick up this discussion again.
I won't let that happen.
Here's hoping.

recs.name: Journey's Footnote
recs.tag: All we can do is to focus on what we can see.

lines.x: Five years ago, the town of Deeproot was destroyed by a Catastrophe.
Thanks to assistance from the Holy City, we were able to rebuild our lives on this new land.
Five years later, the new Deeproot is up on its feet. We are now in a position to revive our town's traditional art—sculpture.
In the old days, the middle of town always displayed the masterwork of our greatest craftsmen.
And now, I would like to revive this tradition and commission a new statue by our best craftsmen, in memory of those who did not survive.
Your father was the best craftsman in town, Susan, and we have seen how hard you've worked to carry his mantle. Will you take up this responsibility?
I—if Father was still here, there would have been no one more qualified.
But for me... I don't know if I'm ready.
It's such a heavy burden, to commemorate the departed.
I know it's a monumental challenge, but there's no other—
If Susan isn't sure, may I try my hand at it?
Melissa! You're back from Laterano?
Your letter said the town was planning to erect a new statue. I set out as soon as I read it.
I went back to the Holy City with the emissaries, but my heart has always been in Deeproot.
Good, very good.
You say you want to work on the statue?
Yes. I honed my skills in Laterano, waiting for the day when I could contribute to the town again.
That's very kind of you. In that case...
Wait!
It was my father who made the statue that stood in the middle of town, before it was destroyed by Catastrophe.
It was... special. Everyone in town said they smelled a scent that belonged only to us when they were near it.
I believe... the best way to commemorate them is to recreate the same statue.
Can you recreate the scent, though?
I-I'm not sure, but I'll try.
Listen, Susan.
The townsfolk, the ones who are left anyway, won't wait for you to rediscover this 'special' tradition.
Sometimes, it's the continuation that matters.
...I know.
(Mutters) The place that Father used to go all the time...
(Mutters) It's dangerous, but...
Susan! Where are you going?
She's headed toward... was I too harsh? I'll bring her back—
I'll take care of Susan.
Is that—Mostima?!
Mostima?!
Mayor, Melissa. How long as it been?
It's good to see you. How are the rest of your team, Andoain and the others?
Heh... they're good.
You...
Let's talk later.
You're Melissa, right? You must be!
You're—
I brought you the materials you needed for the sculpture!
By the way, have you seen a Sankta by the name of Mostima?
(Mutters) Did you pick this time to come back on purpose, Mostima?
Huh?
Where did Mostima go?
She went into the hills.
Won't be back for a while.
Ah—alright.
I'll help out here, then!
You'll just do whatever she dumps on you?
I've been looking for her for a while.
Every time I go to a new place, I happen across something like this, something that's just as much fun as looking for her.
Sounds like she's doing it on purpose.
Who knows? But that's just Mostima.
When we were little, she never came along when I asked her to blow stuff up with me.
But there were a few times when I realized that she was watching me from a distance.
Heh.
How do you know Mostima?
Our town, Deeproot, was destroyed by a Catastrophe five years ago.
My father and I were the only surviving Sanktas.
The Holy City received my father's call for help and sent a squad to pick us up.
(My sister's old squad...)
But their leader, Andoain, didn't just take us away.
Together with his cohorts, he escorted the non-Sankta refugees to this place.
They also requested supplies from the Holy City. It's only later that I learned they had taken out a year's wages in advance to do this.

lines.st: You asked me why my brow is furrowed, Mostima.
I ask you instead: Can you look at yourself in the mirror, and see no shame or regret?
This is all we can do for these non-Sankta refugees.
All we can do is to take them to a patch of new soil, send them some supplies, and take our own people back to Laterano.
What happens here is none of our concern. There's a life of beauty and happiness waiting for us back home.
This has been taken for granted.
We've accepted it, and so have they.

lines.x: El should have started working at Melissa's place now.
Melissa knows enough of my past to satisfy her a bit.
Found you, Susan.
My father used to come here.
You could see the whole town from this place.
Whenever he was in a bad mood, he would come here and look out at the town in the distance.
He used to say that memory isn't just the storage of information. He wanted those who touched the statue to recall the scent of the old days.
But, Father... all I see when I stand here now is a broken ruin.
That statue, it's damaged, but still standing.
I'll be right back.
Wow, this is a huge rock.
It's not just for one statue, is it?
Correct. My plan is to sculpt a set of statues to commemorate the dead.
You've seen similar sets of statues in Laterano, haven't you?
Oh, like the ones on the plaza?
Yes. I wanted to sculpt a set of statues like those, and inscribe the names of the dead.
Sounds like the murals in the churches.
You're a smart girl.
You said you started sculpting only after you went back to Laterano?
Yes. Deeproot was known for its sculptures, but not everyone was a sculptor.
I was one of the non-sculptors.
Honestly, I had difficulty adjusting to life in Laterano.
Maybe I'd just been used to Deeproot, so the constant joyful jubilation in Laterano hardly feels right to me.
Ah—I get that.
I've been following Mostima's trail for a couple of years, and seen a lot of places outside of Laterano. I've come to realize that they're very different from the Holy City.
You know, one of my dreams is to live in a different city.
Then you're not just a happy-go-lucky girl, are you?
Anyway, it wasn't until I went to Laterano that I became interested in sculpting, and began to pursue it formally.
In my heart, I always wanted to come back here.
But Lateran sculptures aren't the same as the ones here, are they?
...I know that.
When I began to seriously study sculpture, I also began to regret not studying Deeproot sculpting while the town was still around.
The past can't be changed, though. I'll continue the tradition here with Lateran techniques.
Unless somebody knows a better way.
So you're hoping Susan succeeds?
...You must be joking. I won't let five years of hard work go to waste.
The largest rock over here.
Gotcha.
Anyway, if you want to help, you can start by cutting the rocks down to the required size.
In Lateran terms—
Blow 'em up!
*sigh* I knew it. Just don't go too far and turn it into a heap of rubble.
Don't worry, I'm an explosives expert!
Time has taken its toll on the streets, which are filled with mud and scattered bricks and rubble. The marks left by Catastrophe are everywhere.
Even the most experienced Messengers avoid such places, but Mostima steps inside without hesitation, stopping only to tighten her hood.
She has gotten far too used to such environments in the span of just two years.
Five years ago, she would not have gone to such lengths. Indeed, she might not have stood here at all.
In the two years that she has been a Legatus, however, she has seen too many places and things that she had never seen before.
When she set foot in the place, she already had an inkling of what Susan was talking about.
The answer to the scent might be a simple one.
You think so too, don't you?
Mostima comes before the statue that stands in the middle of the ruins, carefully removes a broken piece, and takes a sniff of it.
Then, she bends down and picks up a handful of soil, and takes a sniff from it as well.
It is as she thought.
The secret to this 'scent of the town' is simple—
It is a mingled scent of the soil and the stone used in sculpting.
And there is no great secret to why the townsfolk found it familiar. It has the freshness that the vegetation left in the soil, and the unique mineral scent of the stone.
The townsfolk have lived side-by-side with these scents all their lives, which combined to become a scent that brought back memories to the people who lived here.
Can't say it's that pleasant.
Then again, we've been all over, but we've never smelled a smell quite like it, have we?
Explosives, set.
I've done the math. You'll get the result you want when it goes off!
You really know what you're doing, don't you? Couldn't tell at first glance.
I told you, I'm an explosives expert!
Let's get started! Boom!
Lemuel's math was on-point.
The massive rock cracks into several pieces as the explosions go off.
The only thing she neglected was the nature of the stone.
By the way, did I tell you that these rocks emit a large amount of dust when detonated?
Lemuel cannot open her eyes in the thick dust that fills the entire area.
I-I can't see!
What the...?
Mosti—
Shh—
I can't see! Melissa, help!
Look out! There's a hole in the ground—
Huh? Whoa—!
Lemuel's foot finds nothing but empty air. Her body instantly thrown off balance.
As she is about to fall into the hole, a hand grabs her arm and pulls her back.
Thanks, Melissa—
Gotta be more careful, El.
Mostima?!
Hearing the familiar voice, Lemuel rubs her eyes and forces them open.
But she sees no one before her.
*cough* *cough* Mostima?!
Melissa? Was Mostima just here a moment ago?
Melissa? Where did you go?
What's going on?!!
This scent...
Yes, that's it... mm... oh...
It's exactly what Deeproot used to smell like...
This is the scent alright.
I didn't think it would be so simple.
It's the simplest things that leave the deepest impression.
I... have to thank you for finding it, Mostima, Susan.
It's me who should be thanking you, Melissa.
Without you, I would still be going around in circles.
Well, it's a little too early to celebrate.
If the secret behind the scent is so simple, there's no reason why I can't use it.
Now ain't that a cunning move.
You didn't think the townsfolk would pick you just because you discovered the scent?
No, I'll sculpt the best statue!
I don't know how to thank you, Mostima. You helped the town discover that familiar scent, and brought vitality back to the place.
You flatter me, Mr. Mayor... I just happened to be in the right place at the right time.
But I'm curious, Mostima.
Five years ago, all you did was follow your squad leader Andoain, without saying a single word.
Why did you come today to do all this for us?
When she arrived on scene, what she saw was a gravely injured Lemuen, and a crazed Andoain who had committed the act.
She sensed many emotions in that instant—bewilderment, hysteria, alongside relief and acceptance.
It put a doubt in her heart, but did not stop her from acting.
To stop Andoain, she had to knock the Lock and Key from his hand with her patron firearm. She left with Lemuen after retrieving the Lock and Key.
They returned to Laterano, accompanied by Fiammetta.
After that, the Lock and Key were taken from her, and she was put under house arrest.
She did not regret her fall. It was what Andoain saw in the Lock and Key that she was more concerned about.
She made the bold decision to break into the Curia.
Miss this chance, and the secret may elude her forever.
Infiltrating the Curia was not easy, but she succeeded.
Thinking back now, the white-bearded old man must have had a hand in it. He would hardly have allowed Mostima to keep the Lock and Key otherwise.
Whatever the reason, she was once again in possession of the Lock and Key.
The Lock and Key did not react when she took them from Andoain.
This time, when she touched them again with questions in her heart, she walked into a fantastical plane.
There, she saw—
A gap in the past. A cross-section of the future.
She has a pretty good guess as to what Andoain saw.
When she saw what she saw on that plane, she immediately understood why Andoain went mad.
After all, Andoain was always worried about the future, always lamenting over the smallest of tragedies.
In a way, she could even say that Fiammetta's anger at Andoain's actions was born out of Fiammetta's approval of him—

Considering Fiammetta's sense of justice, it is no wonder that she always held Andoain in high regard for the concern he showed for others, in comparison to Fiammetta herself, who always seemed a little aloof and removed.
However, Mostima was not obsessed with the reasons for Andoain's madness. It was not simply because of the emotions that she sensed from the pair at that instant.
Instead, it is because she had a feeling, a feeling that she had perhaps harbored from the moment she joined Andoain's squad, even the moment she first saw Andoain—
They were walking divergent paths, and it was inevitable that they must go their separate ways.

It was like the many thousands of pieces before her eyes, each one potentially revealing the answer to a question. Perhaps the answer to the ultimate question will reveal itself when all the pieces are exhausted.
Andoain will choose to walk toward those pieces without hesitation, stepping into the dark mire where the stars shine.
As for her—she chose to turn back.
When I saw what I saw, I thought—
Oh, how terrible.
I didn't feel anything else.
That's why I didn't understand the struggle that a certain somebody was going through.
But now—
Mostima, those horns...
Are you fallen?!
These past two years, I've traveled the lands as a Legatus, and I've come to a conclusion—
Lovely bastards, the Sanktas are.
I've just relearned how to live with this land, after realizing that I was a bastard.
Tell El that I have a new mission. I'll be in Lungmen for a while.
I ran into this guy by the name of 'Emperor' six months ago. He's in Lungmen too. I think I'll pay him a visit.
Mostima turns around at the hillside.
She can see the town square in the distance.
Susan and Melissa have already started their preparations. A crowd has assembled to watch them, and it is growing bigger.
The red hair of a certain Sankta stands out in the crowd. She goes from one side to another, helping out here and there, seemingly having forgotten why she was here in the first place.
For once, Mostima is not wearing her hood. She lets the breeze brush against her cheeks and run through her hair.

lines.st: I think I understand you a little better now, Andoain.
Maybe I should have had a few more drinks with you. Maybe I should have let you have more time together with Lemuen.
Alright, I know, you were always going to leave in the end.
But there's something that I want to say.
Now that I've gotten to know you better, I can say with certainty—
I won't make the same choices you did.
Nothing can bear the burden of the happiness of all the people. Not you, not me, not even Laterano.
All we can do is to focus on what we can see.
Just like I've been taking El around these past two years, fulfilling a little of the responsibility I bear for her coming out of Laterano to find me. That's all.
I don't hate you like Fiammetta does. But don't expect a warm welcome when we meet again.
Wherever that might be, our journey will take us there.
